chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal al-Asadi, from Tha'labah ibn Maymun, from Abd al-A'la ibn A'yun, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him)

regarding this verse: 'Had it been a near advantage and a short journey, they would certainly have followed you, but the tedious journey was too long for them; and they swear by Allah: If we had been able, we would certainly have gone forth with you; they cause their own souls to perish, and Allah knows that they are most surely liars.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They indeed had the ability, and it was known that had it been a near advantage and a short journey, they would have done so.'

key_terms.يَهْلِكُونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ: they cause their own souls to perish

ai.seo_question: Why did the Hypocrites fail to join the Prophet's expedition if they were physically able?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the verse regarding the Hypocrites of Tabuk, clarifying that their failure to join was not due to a lack of physical capability but stemmed from their insincerity and divine foreknowledge of their true disposition. This interpretation underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between external ability and internal conviction, highlighting that the 'distance' mentioned in the verse refers to the spiritual gap of their hypocrisy rather than mere geographical hardship.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 15. My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) both said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of `Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal al-Asadi, on the authority of Tha`labah ibn Maymun, on the authority of `Abd Al-A`la ibn A`yun, that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) asked to interpret this verse: Had it been a near advantage and a short journey, they would certainly have followed you, but the tedious journey was too long for them; and they swear by Allah: If we had been able, we would certainly have gone forth with you; they cause their own souls to perish, and Allah knows that they are most surely liars.
He (AS) said: “They indeed had the ability. Allah knew that they would have carried out their duty had it been a short and advantageous journey.”
